header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rem:anonymous:m153:norm, from the Referenzkorpus Mittelhochdeutsch, ReM 2.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.68v.1: mort is an unidentified horse disease; Fases is an unidentified name. sluhtere is taken as swaddling bands. übervangen is taken as founder; geræhe may be founder too, or stiffness of the limbs; wambîzic ('belly-biting') is taken as colic.

nodes.text: For the plague of a horse which is called *mort*. Say: John was a man; Fases his son recovered from it; so may this horse [recover] from the *mort*. The Our Father, three times.
Likewise, for a foundered horse. Say: Christ was born on earth, thrown into a manger, bound in swaddling bands, soon lost;
may holy Christ cure this horse, N., of founder, of *geræhe*, of the colic, of the worm, and
is harming it. In the name
of the Lord. May it be for your cure.
The Our Father; after that, the same three times.
